about: Homework for this pillar, one list per AI (Claude writes it; tools/kit/render.py in jpavia10/prometheus-hub turns it into docs/agents/QUEUE_{ai}.md and the Drive docs). Every task says exactly what to read, what to make, how many, where to save it, how Claude checks it and what makes it not done. A task is done only when the file passes the checks, never because it was sent.

tasks.title: Argus Album: the spec sheet (every photo the pillars use: Titan's coin photos (titan-photos-as/eu/na), Hearth's room photos, Apollo's progress photos; one album, tagged by pillar)
tasks.why: Argus Album is a seat on the desk with no page yet. Joseph wants each pillar developed on its own; the first step is a spec Claude can build from.
steps: Write the spec for Argus Album: every photo the pillars use: Titan's coin photos (titan-photos-as/eu/na), Hearth's room photos, Apollo's progress photos; one album, tagged by pillar.
At least 6 data sources with their real API names and documentation URLs (open each one); say plainly when something has no public API.
Four first screens, each listing every number on it and where it comes from.
Five 'done when' checks that can be tested on a phone.
Photo location data (EXIF GPS) is stripped before anything is public.

deliver.shape: one markdown file with these 6 headings, in this order: 1 Purpose (one sentence) | 2 Data sources (a table: source | what it gives | how to get it (API name) | docs URL | sign-in type | cost | limits) | 3 First four screens (for each: its name, every number and list on it, where each comes from) | 4 Version 1 done when (5 checks Claude can test) | 5 Privacy (what never leaves the device) | 6 What Joseph must do once (accounts, keys, apps)

tasks.done_when: All 6 headings, at least 6 sources with working docs URLs, 4 screens, 5 testable checks.
checks: Claude checks each 'done when' can be tested without asking Joseph.
rejected_if: a row copied from another row with the names changed
a source URL that does not open or does not say what the row claims
fewer items than the count
a file saved anywhere but the folder named here, or under another name
an API that does not exist or a docs URL for something else
a screen that lists a number with no source

tasks.title: 40 photo metadata tags that leak location or identity
tasks.why: Argus strips EXIF and GPS from every photo it keeps; Claude needs the full list to test the strip.
steps: From exiftool.org/TagNames (EXIF, GPS, XMP, IPTC, MakerNotes pages) and the EXIF 2.32 spec: 40 tags that reveal where, when, who or which device (GPSLatitude, GPSLongitude, GPSAltitude, DateTimeOriginal, SerialNumber, BodySerialNumber, LensSerialNumber, OwnerName, Artist, XMP dc:creator, IPTC By-line, ...).
For each: tag ID in hex (when it has one), name, group, what it leaks, the URL.
tasks.done_when: 40 tags, every ID and name as on exiftool.org.
checks: Claude compares every row with exiftool.org.
rejected_if: fewer rows than the count, or a row missing a field of the shape
a row copied from another row with the names changed
a URL that does not open, is a front page or a search page, or does not say what the row claims
a quote that is not on the page it cites (Claude opens 10 rows at random)
a file saved anywhere but the folder named here, or under another name
a tag ID that does not match its name

tasks.title: The coin photo standard: 20 rules from professional numismatic photography
tasks.why: Titan's Phase 2 pro photos (Argus keeps them) need one written standard before Joseph shoots 339 coins.
steps: 20 rules (lighting angle, light type, background, lens, aperture, focus stacking, white balance, scale, orientation, file format, resolution, toning, glare on proof coins, holder glare, ...), each from a named source: a numismatic photography book with page, PCGS or NGC imaging pages, the ANA, or a museum imaging guide.
For each: the rule as a number or a yes/no where possible (e.g. 'light at 15-30 degrees from the coin face'), the source and the quote.

deliver.shape: [{"n":1,"rule":"light the coin from 15-30 degrees above the face","value":{"min_deg":15,"max_deg":30},"source":"...","url":"https://...","quote":"..."}]

tasks.done_when: 20 rules, each quoted from a numismatic or museum source.
rejected_if: fewer rows than the count, or a row missing a field of the shape
a row copied from another row with the names changed
a URL that does not open, is a front page or a search page, or does not say what the row claims
a quote that is not on the page it cites (Claude opens 10 rows at random)
a file saved anywhere but the folder named here, or under another name
a rule from a general photography blog

tasks.title: Image formats on Android Chrome: 6 formats x 3 browser features
tasks.why: Argus decides which format to store photos in on the phone.
steps: Formats: WebP, AVIF, HEIC, JPEG XL, PNG, JPEG. Features: shows in , decodes with createImageBitmap, encodes with canvas.toBlob(type).
For each of the 18 cells: yes / no / partial for Chrome for Android, the version it started, the caniuse.com or MDN URL and the quote.
tasks.done_when: 18 cells, each quoted from caniuse or MDN.

tasks.title: 6 perceptual hash methods: steps, threshold, source
tasks.why: Argus (and Titan's dupes.py) should find the same coin photographed twice.
steps: Methods: aHash, dHash, pHash (DCT), wHash (wavelet), blockhash, colour-moment hash.

For each: the steps numbered (resize size, colour, transform, bits), the hash length in bits, the Hamming distance below which two photos count as the same with its source, and a reference (paper DOI, the author's page, or the ImageHash library docs).

deliver.shape: [{"n":1,"method":"dHash","steps":["grayscale","resize to 9x8","compare each pixel to its right neighbour","64 bits"],"bits":64,"same_below":10,"threshold_source":"...","url":"https://...","quote":"..."}]

tasks.done_when: 6 methods; Claude implements each from the steps and runs it on 20 Titan photo pairs.
checks: A method whose steps cannot be implemented as written fails the row.

tasks.title: Argus Album: second reader on Gemini's spec
tasks.why: Every source in a spec gets a second reader before Claude builds on it.
inputs: Gemini's file argus_gemini_spec_*.md in the incoming folder (once it is there)
steps: Open every data source's docs URL; for each write: source, Gemini's claim (sign-in, cost, limits), what the page says, agree/differ.
Add up to 5 sources Gemini missed, same columns.

deliver.shape: table: source | gemini says | page says | url | agree/differ
